title: Rotthaus criterion from finitely many contracted principal boundaries
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], $x\in B$, and assume $B$ is $(x)$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Assume additionally that $B/xB$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Let $\mathfrak n$ be a maximal ideal and set $C=\varprojlim_j B_{\mathfrak n}/x^jB_{\mathfrak n}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $\mathfrak s$ be a minimal singular prime of $C$, meaning $C_{\mathfrak s}$ is not regular local and every localization at a strictly smaller prime is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $\Gamma(\mathfrak n)$ be the finite sets $\gamma\subseteq\operatorname{Max}B$ containing $\mathfrak n$. Put $B_\gamma=(B\setminus\bigcup_{\mathfrak a\in\gamma}\mathfrak a)^{-1}B$, $D_\gamma=\varprojlim_j B_\gamma/x^jB_\gamma$, and $\mathfrak s_\gamma=\mathfrak s\cap D_\gamma$ under the canonical map $D_\gamma\to C$. Let $E_\gamma$ be the integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] of $D_\gamma/\mathfrak s_\gamma$ in its fraction field. Define
$$\Delta_\gamma(x)=\{\mathfrak Q\cap B:\mathfrak Q\text{ is a prime minimal over }xE_\gamma\},\qquad \Delta(x)=\bigcup_{\gamma\in\Gamma(\mathfrak n)}\Delta_\gamma(x).$$
If $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak s_\gamma>0$ for every $\gamma$ and $\Delta(x)$ is finite, then $\mathfrak s\cap B\ne(0)$. Heights are local Krull dimensions [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.3 (Rotthaus Hilfssatz), printed p.11, citing Nishimura–Nishimura Theorem 1.9 and Proposition 1.18; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: Argue by contradiction, assuming $\mathfrak s\cap B=0$. Then $B$ injects into the domain $C/\mathfrak s$, so $B$ is a domain and $\mathfrak s_\gamma\cap B=0$ for every $\gamma$. If $x=0$, then $D_\gamma=B_\gamma$; a prime of this localization contracting to zero is zero (if $a/u$ belongs to it, then so does $a$, hence $a=0$). This contradicts positive height. Thus $x\ne0$ and $x\notin\mathfrak s_\gamma$. Also $x$ lies in every maximal ideal of $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical], hence is not a unit because $\mathfrak n$ exists.

source.place: Theorem 1.9, reduction preceding Lemma 1.10; zero case written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-bounded-formal-singular-primes-stabilize] to $A=B$: Noetherianity, the Nagata property, completeness and the G-ring property of $B/xB$ are hypotheses; Step 1 gives the zero contraction and $x\ne0$, and the stated singular prime and boundary set agree literally. Obtain $\gamma_0$ with $\mathfrak s_\gamma=\mathfrak s_\delta D_\gamma$ for $\gamma_0\subseteq\gamma\subseteq\delta$. Restrict to these finite subsets; their boundary union is still finite. Contraction compatibility follows by composing the canonical maps to $C$.

Apply [lem-per-bounded-normalization-limit-finite] to this restricted family. Step 1 supplies the domain and nonzero nonunit conditions, Step 2 supplies extension and contraction compatibility, and the finite boundary hypothesis persists. Its normalization rings are exactly the given $E_\gamma$. Thus $B\to T=\varprojlim_{\gamma\supseteq\gamma_0}E_\gamma$ is injective and module-finite, and every minimal prime of $xT$ contracts into the restricted boundary union. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], $T$ is integral over $B$.

Choose a prime $P$ minimal over $xB$ by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal]; Step 1 ensures that ideal is proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] a prime $q'$ of $T$ contracts to $P$. Since $x\in q'$, [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] gives $xT\subseteq q\subseteq q'$ with $q$ minimal over $xT$. Then $x\in q\cap B\subseteq P$, so minimality of $P$ forces $q\cap B=P$. Step 3's boundary assertion gives a finite $\gamma\supseteq\gamma_0$ and a prime $Q$ minimal over $xE_\gamma$ whose contraction to $B$ is $P$.

source.place: End of proof of Theorem 1.9, p.460; lying-over and minimal-prime selection made explicit.

proof.text: Put $q_\gamma=Q\cap D_\gamma$. It contains $x$ and $\mathfrak s_\gamma$, and contracts to $P$. The projection in [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] for $N=1$ identifies $D_\gamma/xD_\gamma$ with $B_\gamma/xB_\gamma$. Hence primes of $D_\gamma$ containing $x$ correspond to primes of $B$ containing $x$ and disjoint from the denominators of $B_\gamma$: inverse images under the quotient maps give the first correspondence; for localization, $a/u$ belongs to a prime exactly when $a/1$ does, giving the second. These operations preserve and reflect inclusion. If a prime $r\subseteq q_\gamma$ contains $x$, its contraction lies between $xB$ and $P$, hence equals $P$ by minimality. The correspondence then gives $r=q_\gamma$. Thus $q_\gamma$ is minimal over $xD_\gamma$.

source.place: End of proof of Theorem 1.9, p.460; principal-quotient argument replaces a catenary height comparison.

proof.text: The ring $B_\gamma$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], and $D_\gamma$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. Therefore [lem-sfb-krull-principal-ideal-height-bound] gives $\operatorname{ht}q_\gamma\le1$. But $x\notin\mathfrak s_\gamma$ by Step 1 and $x\in q_\gamma$, so $\mathfrak s_\gamma\subsetneq q_\gamma$. Positive height of $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ supplies a prime $r\subsetneq\mathfrak s_\gamma$ by the definition of height; the chain $r\subsetneq\mathfrak s_\gamma\subsetneq q_\gamma$ has length two, a contradiction. Consequently $\mathfrak s\cap B\ne0$.

source.place: End of proof of Theorem 1.9, p.460; final height contradiction.

proof_origin.place: Assembly from Proposition 1.18 and the normalization-limit portion of Theorem 1.9; final contradiction by principal ideal height, without catenarity.
